subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Should OpenClaw allow provider conversion to hide any ordinary tool-result content, or should cache-safe summarization be limited to explicitly nonessential heartbeat/status tools?
rationale: The linked issue is real, but choosing which tool outputs may be removed from the model-visible prompt changes core agent behavior and cannot be settled by a broad hard-coded list in a stale branch.

options.title: Require narrow rework before merge
options.body: Keep ordinary exec/read/web/memory results visible, move the fix to current packages/ai provider files, and only summarize explicitly nonessential heartbeat/status outputs with live proof.

options.title: Pause for broader policy
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers define a general tool-result visibility lifecycle for cache-sensitive providers.

options.title: Accept broad suppression intentionally
options.body: Maintainers may accept that ordinary tool outputs become placeholders, but that would trade cache stability for degraded agent reasoning and should be explicit.

recommendation.title: Require narrow rework before merge
recommendation.body: Keep ordinary exec/read/web/memory results visible, move the fix to current packages/ai provider files, and only summarize explicitly nonessential heartbeat/status outputs with live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has adjacent provider/prompt-cache history and is the best available owner for the provider-cache policy choice.
